rv.q: What follows are two hours of the craziest kind of fun you can imagine, with a very clever script and a cast to match.
The zany show-within-a-show is written by Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer and Henry Shields (“The Play That Goes Wrong”) and follows the Cornley University Drama Society.
If farce is not to your taste, you should give “Peter Pan Goes Wrong” a very wide berth.
The problem with Peter Pan Goes Wrong is that we see every joke coming from a mile away, sapping it of all its humor before it arrives.

cn.t: Critics are split: two rave about the Lyric Stage's wildly fun, laugh-out-loud physical comedy, while one finds the chaos falls flat. Audience energy runs high, but execution divides opinion.
